[id="agent-state-storage-backend-comparison_{context}"]
= Agent state storage backend comparison

[role="_abstract"]
You can choose from several storage backends for LangGraph agent state persistence on {productname-long}.
Each backend offers different trade-offs for latency, durability, scaling, and operational complexity.
The following tables help you select the right backend for your workload requirements.

== Storage backend comparison

The following table compares the available storage backends for LangGraph agent state.

.Agent state storage backend comparison
[cols="1,1,1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Backend
|Latency
|Durability
|Scaling
|Persistence across pod restarts
|Recommended use case

|MemorySaver (in-memory)
|Sub-millisecond
|None -- all data is lost when the process exits
|Single process only
|No
|Local development and testing

|SQLite
|Low (local filesystem)
|Persists to local file -- lost if the pod's filesystem is ephemeral
|Single process only -- does not support concurrent access from multiple pods
|Only with a persistent volume
|Local development and single-pod testing

|PostgreSQL
|Low to moderate (network round-trip)
|Full ACID durability with write-ahead logging
|Supports multiple concurrent pods -- horizontal scaling is possible
|Yes
|Production deployments on {productname-short}

|Redis
|Sub-millisecond to low (network round-trip)
|Configurable -- depends on Redis persistence settings (RDB, AOF, or both)
|Supports multiple concurrent pods -- horizontal scaling with Redis Cluster
|Yes, when Redis persistence is enabled
|High-throughput production workloads that require low checkpoint latency
|===

== Llama Stack memory API compatibility

Not all storage backends are supported through the Llama Stack memory API.
The following table shows which backends are available for each persistence layer.

.Llama Stack memory API compatibility by backend
[cols="1,1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Backend
|Llama Stack `persistence_store` (agent metadata)
|Llama Stack `responses_store` (response history)
|LangGraph checkpointer (graph checkpoints)

|MemorySaver
|No
|No
|Yes -- via `langgraph.checkpoint.memory.MemorySaver`

|SQLite
|Yes -- set `type: sqlite` in `run.yaml`
|Yes -- set `type: sqlite` in `run.yaml`
|Yes -- via `langgraph.checkpoint.sqlite.SqliteSaver` (requires the `langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite` package)

|PostgreSQL
|Yes -- set `type: postgres` in `run.yaml`
|Yes -- set `type: postgres` in `run.yaml`
|Yes -- via `langgraph.checkpoint.postgres.PostgresSaver`

|Redis
|No
|No
|Yes -- via `langgraph.checkpoint.redis.RedisSaver`
|===

[NOTE]
====
The Llama Stack `persistence_store` and `responses_store` require either SQLite or PostgreSQL.
If you use Redis for LangGraph checkpoints, you must still configure PostgreSQL or SQLite for the Llama Stack metadata stores.
====

== When to use PostgreSQL or Redis

PostgreSQL is the recommended backend for most production deployments on {productname-short}.
PostgreSQL provides full ACID compliance, integrates with {productname-short} backup and monitoring infrastructure, and can serve as both the Llama Stack metadata store and the LangGraph checkpoint store.

Redis is appropriate when your workload requires checkpoint latency under 1 millisecond and you can accept the additional operational complexity of managing a separate Redis deployment alongside PostgreSQL.

Consider the following factors when choosing between PostgreSQL and Redis:

.Decision factors for PostgreSQL or Redis
[cols="1,1,1", options="header"]
|===
|Factor
|PostgreSQL
|Redis

|Operational simplicity
|Single database for all state layers
|Requires both Redis and PostgreSQL

|Checkpoint latency
|Low to moderate (1-5 ms typical)
|Sub-millisecond to low (<1 ms typical)

|Durability guarantees
|Full ACID -- every committed transaction is durable
|Configurable -- RDB snapshots can lose up to the last snapshot interval

|Backup integration
|Standard PostgreSQL backup tools (pg_dump, WAL archiving)
|Requires Redis-specific backup procedures

|Scaling approach
|Vertical scaling -- read replicas for read-heavy workloads
|Horizontal scaling with Redis Cluster for high-throughput workloads

|{productname-short} integration
|Supported as Llama Stack metadata store and LangGraph checkpointer
|Supported as LangGraph checkpointer only
|===
